messages:
carmen: Quick question / proposal — we should explicitly surface failover semantics between v1 and v2 in the console and API docs. Right now teams assume 'v2 preferred, fall back to v1 on error', but there are subtle behaviors (quota counting, billing tag, and telemetry attribution) that aren't obvious. :thinking:
eli: +1. we've had at least two customer tickets where requests silently went to v1 during a routing spike and they saw token billing differences. need to clarify both the runtime behaviour and the user-facing affordance.
sam.k: Agreed. Concrete ask: 1) Console copy that shows "If this route falls back to v1 you'll be billed at v1 rates" or similar, 2) an opt-in toggle for "never fallback" at route level, 3) telemetry flag so we can attribute which model actually served the request.
carmen: I like the 'never fallback' toggle as a per-route policy. UX question: toggle should default OFF? my gut says OFF to preserve availability for apps that prefer correctness over strict model.
anya: Can we do three-tier policy instead? prefer-v2 (default), prefer-availability (fallback allowed), strict-version (reject/404). That maps to current routing modes and makes semantics explicit.
eli: Also need to address quota semantics. If a request is routed to v1, which quota is decremented? customer quota should be on the route + effective model tag so billing matches. We should not silently charge v1 cents while reporting tokens to v2 telemetry.
infra-bot: Runtime note: current router has a soft-fallback at 95th percentile latency/pressure threshold. We can expose that threshold and make it configurable per-tenant, but toggling to strict will bypass fallback.
sam.k: For API-level opt-ins, we can introduce an opt-in header for clients: `X-Redwood-Fallback: allow|prefer-availability|deny`. Example: `X-Redwood-Fallback: deny` => route returns 409 if v2 capacity unavailable.
anya: Need to document how SDKs should behave when they get 409 vs when requests succeed but to different model. SDKs might want to surface a structured result: {served_model: "redwood-v1.3", intended_model: "redwood-v2", billed_at: "v1-rate"}. That would make debugging much easier.
eli: Telemetry: add a top-level tag `served_model` and `routing_decision` (fallback, canary, pinned) to traces and logs. Also add a delta-meter: tokens_billed_vs_tokens_intended to catch regressions.
anya: UX: console should show recent fallback events per-route with time, served_model, reason (capacity|error|timeout), and an action to pin route to a model or flip strict mode.
carmen: Ops question: what's the rollout plan for this? we need to avoid breaking customers who rely on current silent fallback. propose 3 phased rollout: 1) telemetry + console visibility (no behavior change), 2) introduce opt-in header and per-route toggle (off by default), 3) make stricter controls GA and add console nudges.
sam.k: Sounds right. For phase 1 we must ensure metrics are exported to tenant dashboards so CSMs can reach out proactively.
eli: Also add a small migration guide for customers: detect silent fallback, how to pin, how to opt-in to deny fallback, and cost implications.
anya: blocker: we need to ensure billing pipeline can accept model-level rate tags. Finance OK with this?
deploy-bot: @finance-team FYI — new routing telemetry fields proposed: served_model, routing_decision, billed_rate_tag. Please ack if fine.
infra-bot: I'll open an infra RFC with runtime changes, config knobs, and feature flags. Will include sample header handling pseudocode: ```
if header == "deny" and no_v2_capacity:
  return 409, {"error":"v2-unavailable: fallback-denied"}
else if header == "prefer-availability" and no_v2_capacity:
  route_to(v1)
else:
  route_to(v2)
```
carmen: ok great — I'll draft console copy and a short customer-facing FAQ. Anyone want to pair on the RFC review?
eli: I can review the infra RFC first pass.
sam.k: I'll draft the SDK changes and sample response payload.
anya: I'll work on telemetry and the console mockups.
carmen: thanks all :+1:
